strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a concern on this abrasive Curitiba surface, so managing the rubber is key.
With a lap length of 3.695 km, fuel consumption will be a critical factor, especially in the closing stages.
The pit window is likely to be relatively short here, meaning teams will need to execute quick and efficient stops.
An early safety car could shake things up, forcing teams to react and adjust their strategies on the fly.
The balance between straight-line speed and cornering grip is crucial here, influencing the downforce levels chosen by the teams.
Running a long first stint could prove beneficial, but it comes with the risk of getting caught out by a safety car.
The relatively short lap means traffic management will be a challenge, especially for those starting further back.
The undercut could be powerful here, with drivers able to gain significant time in clear air after a pit stop.
weatherCommentary: The weather in Curitiba can be unpredictable, with sunshine one minute and rain the next.

The humidity is high today, which will make things even tougher for the drivers inside the cockpit.

The wind direction can also play a role, affecting the car's balance and making certain corners more challenging.
